note: 'CNMC and Yunnan Copper Industry is set to commission a US$300 million copper smelter in Zambia's Chambishi town.' Same $300m figure repeated by Mining.com (https://www.mining.com/the-mad-scramble-for-copper/), which dates commissioning to 2013; first phase actually opened 2009.

source_name: China Nonferrous Mining Corporation Ltd (CNMC) company profile
note: Phase 1: 150,000 t blister copper + 400,000 t sulphuric acid per year.

unit: tonnes blister/anode copper per annum (post Phase 2)
source_name: China Nonferrous Mining Corporation Ltd (CNMC) company profile
note: After Phase 2 expansion: 250,000 t blister/anode copper, 600,000 t sulphuric acid, 17,500 t cobalt-copper alloy, 300 t bismuth oxychloride per year. Phase 2 expansion cost not found in a citable source.

Verified on ERG page: '6,800 tpa cobalt metal', acquired 2010, currently on care and maintenance. ZCCM-IH 10% stake per Investing News Network (https://investingnews.com/daily/resource-investing/battery-metals-investing/cobalt-investing/erg-chambishi-metals-suspends-cobalt-production-zambia/).

unit: tonnes Grade A copper metal per annum
note: Placed on care and maintenance end-Jan 2020 due to concentrate shortage after Zambia's 5% import duty on concentrates (Mining.com: https://www.mining.com/web/erg-suspends-zambia-refinery-on-shortage-of-cobalt-copper-concentrates-2/). No published financials found.

US$400m investment commitment announced alongside the 2009 acquisition (mine restart + Muliashi development).

entity: Sino-Metals Leach Zambia Ltd (CNMC 55% / HK Zhongfei 30% / NFCA 15%)
note: 'With an investment of about $70 million', Mwambashi Mine targeting 10,000 tpa copper cathode. Company operates Chambishi leach plant since 2006.

Figure surfaced from USGS 2013 Zambia yearbook via search; ownership split (55/30/15) from same source. On 18 Feb 2025 the company's tailings dam collapsed, releasing ~50 million litres of acidic waste into the Kafue river system (Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Sino-Metals_Leach_Zambia_dam_disaster; HRW: https://www.hrw.org/news/2025/09/11/zambia-acid-spill-jeopardizes-residents-health).

EMR Capital acquired 80% of Lubambe from Vale International and African Rainbow Minerals for US$97.1m (announced Aug 2017). Australian Mining reported a $124m headline figure incl. other elements (https://www.australianmining.com.au/emr-secures-124m-copper-acquisition-vale-african-rainbow-minerals/).

JCHX (via Sundimo Mining Investments) acquired EMR's 80% for a nominal '$0.000001 million' — effectively a token price with assumption of the distressed mine's liabilities. ZCCM-IH confirmation: https://diggers.news/business/2024/07/11/zccm-ih-confirms-sale-of-lubambe-to-jchx/. Post-deal restructuring left ZCCM-IH with 30% and JCHX 70% per ZCCM-IH investment page (https://www.zccm-ih.com.zm/investments/mining-assets/lubambe-copper-mines-plc/). The ~$857m figure in the task brief (project debt context) was NOT found in any published source.

JCHX to invest ~US$300m in operations and life-of-mine extension (also https://www.mining-technology.com/news/chinas-jchx-lubambe-copper-mine/; ZCCM-IH statement in diggers.news confirms 'US$300 million into Lubambe').

source_name: ZCCM-IH, Lubambe extract from 2023 Annual Report
note: 14,984 t payable copper vs budget of 22,979 t; production hindered by ground conditions, dewatering, dilution.

unit: tonnes contained copper in concentrate per annum (design)
source_name: ZCCM-IH investment page - Lubambe Copper Mines Plc
note: Concentrator design: 2.5 Mtpa ore at 2.3% Cu yielding 45,000 t contained copper; currently ramping up under JCHX.

unit: tonnes copper in concentrates per annum (approx.)
note: 'The Company currently produces 10 000 tons of copper in concentrates per year.' Mine placed on care & maintenance 1 July 2020, then leased to Lian Chao and Yue Ventures Ltd (LC&Y) per ZCCM-IH annual report summaries (https://www.zccm-ih.com.zm/category/all-posts/investee-companies/annual-report-summaries/page/6/) and Jinchuan (http://en.jnmc.com/2022-06/25/c_784243.htm). NO published sale value for any 2017-2021 ownership transfer was found — the arrangement documented is a lease, not a sale; Jinchuan/ZCCM-IH shareholding unchanged in published sources.
Phase 1 heap leach SX/EW, 10,000 tpa from Dec 2022; first Phase 2 stage doubled capacity to 20,000 tpa (first cathode Jan 2024).

unit: tonnes copper cathode per annum (Phase 2 target)
note: Phase 2 expands to 56,000 tpa via 46,000 tpa agitated leach + SX/EW circuit.
Moxico announced ~$100m investment to expand Mimbula (April 2022).
Mimbula produced ~14 kt copper cathode in 2024.

Ecora Resources $50m producing copper stream on Mimbula, 11-year LOM, copper delivered at 30% of quarterly average LME price. Separately Queen's Road Capital invested US$50m in Moxico Resources plc (https://queensrdcapital.com/news/queens-road-capital-announces-us-50-million-investment-in-moxico-resources-plc/). NO Trafigura deal found in published sources.
